full_judgment: 5. Perused the F.I.R. and other connected papers as available in record with copies of G.D. entries and statements of some of the witnesses recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It appears that an F.I.R. was lodged for the alleged offence under sections 143/447/448/307/326/302/34 of the penal Code wherein the petitioners have been named as accused along with others. It further appears that admittedly the informant-party belongs to ruling political party and that the petitioners are also members of a political party in opposition. The plain reading of the F.I.R. gives us a light about strong political rivalry between the parties. The way in which the F.I.R. has been couched appears to be an work of law knowing persons, furthermore, it appears that some of the witnesses of this case are found to be the witnesses in seven G.D. entries allegedly made whose statement were recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The language of all the seven G.D. entries are found to be the product of some law knowing persons. More so some of them (witnesses) appears to have made their statements under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure implicating the petitioners. The most vital thing in this case is that as regards the threatening or allegation of misuse of privilege of bail as it transpires from the wordings of G.D. entries we may term the same as the outcome of one and single individual. Be the case as it may, the law enforcing agency with whom the G.D. Entries were made appears to be sitting idle thereon and for which we are unable to ascertain as to whether the subject matters of those G.D. entries have got any truth
